title: Fruit Into Baskets / At Most Two Distinct
contract: Find the longest contiguous subarray containing at most two distinct integer values.
brute: int best=0;for(int l=0;l<a.length;l++){Set<Integer> types=new HashSet<>();for(int r=l;r<a.length;r++){types.add(a[r]);if(types.size()>2)break;best=Math.max(best,r-l+1);emit("Try a valid interval","range",new int[]{l,r},"best",best);}}return best;
optimal: Map<Integer,Integer> counts=new HashMap<>();int l=0,best=0;for(int r=0;r<a.length;r++){counts.merge(a[r],1,Integer::sum);while(counts.size()>2){int x=a[l++];counts.put(x,counts.get(x)-1);if(counts.get(x)==0)counts.remove(x);}best=Math.max(best,r-l+1);emit("Restore at most two live keys","range",new int[]{l,r},"counts",counts,"best",best);}return best;
reasoning: Restart the distinct-type set for every starting index.
Maintain value multiplicities so removing a left item deletes a key only when its last occurrence leaves.
At most two distinct is monotone under shrinking. A set without counts cannot tell whether another copy of the departing type remains.
